label: In-root purity of requirements, from purity REQUIRES_LACK_1 and the sense bridge
meaning: Fix an actual root r, a pure determination t of r and a set S of pure determinations. If t required, in r, the lack of S, then by the sense bridge t would require the lack of S as such, which the purity of requirements (0c8631bd) excludes. So the in-root purity premise is no stronger than 0c8631bd together with the bridge. It does not show the converse: a rival that denies the bridge can keep 0c8631bd and deny the in-root premise (simpleUnityCarriageMap, clause 3). No axioms.
